one_sentence_story: When chanting eight random digits aloud failed to crash logical reasoning in 1974, Alan Baddeley and Graham Hitch replaced 'one-shelf short-term memory' with multi-component Working Memory — a Central Executive coordinating a 2-second Phonological Loop, a Visuospatial Sketchpad, and (in 2000) an Episodic Buffer.
so_what_for_you: Match your tools to Baddeley's four rooms: never pit two verbal tasks or two visual tasks against each other at once, and offload long spoken multi-step instructions onto a visible whiteboard sketch so your Central Executive stays free to think.
